title: Inhaled salbutamol induces leanness in well-trained healthy females but not males during a period of endurance training: a randomised controlled trial
authors: Hostrup M, Weinreich C, Bjerre M, Kohlbrenner D, Bangsbo J, Jessen S
population: 19 women and 21 men, well-trained and healthy, inhaling salbutamol 800 to 1600 µg or placebo on training days during combined endurance and high-intensity interval training, double-blind
funder: The study was supported by Anti Doping Denmark; one author was supported by a Postdoc Mobility Fellowship of the Swiss National Science Foundation.
authorConflicts: The authors have no conflicting interests.
result: Salbutamol reduced fat mass in women only (-0.8 kg at 6 weeks against placebo, 95% CI -0.5 to -1.6; sex-by-treatment p = 0.048), with lean mass gain in women. Salbutamol lowered the overall rise in maximal oxygen uptake in both sexes (treatment effect p = 0.014), mainly through a blunted increase over the first 4 weeks, increases being of similar size between treatments by week 6, and lowered quadriceps strength in women by 39 N·m (17 to 61) at 6 weeks; muscle electron transport chain complex I to V abundance rose, while beta2-adrenoceptor protein content was unchanged.
